correctness.rationale: Exact Fourier inversion of balls gives a Bessel integral for every profile. Its uniform large-radius expansion has a spatially Lp-integrable remainder, while two integrations by parts yield profile-uniform tail decay. The logarithmic annular periodic-average computation, uniformly for p=p_c-lambda/log(1/delta), produces the stated analytic coefficient and crossover function; both near-edge errors vanish after division by log(1/delta). d=2 coefficient and the 3D ball integral were independently checked with executable supplemental code. No finite calculation is taken as proof.

value.rationale: For Fourier balls, p_c=2d/(d+1) is the natural transition from finite to divergent unregularized kernel Lp mass. The theorem resolves the exact reciprocal-logarithmic transition window, including both sides of the critical index, with a dimension-explicit function and uniformity over arbitrary normalized, uniformly regular radial profiles that may change with delta. Fixed-exponent prior kernel and operator estimates do not give this window; the result is a motivated universality statement rather than an arbitrary additional number.
